functions.description: The value without its sign. Null for a non-number.
The smallest whole number not less than the value. Null for a non-number.
True when the text contains the part, case-sensitively. A non-text argument makes it false.
True when the text ends with the suffix, case-sensitively. A non-text argument makes it false.
True when both texts are equal, ignoring case. A non-text argument makes it false.
The largest whole number not greater than the value. Null for a non-number.
Formats the number with thousands separators and a fixed number of decimal places (0 to 10), for example 1234.5 with 2 places is 1,234.50.
True for a number, or for text that reads as a finite number such as " 12.5 " or "-3e2". Booleans and null are not numbers.
True when the name or UUID is the player this run belongs to. It does not look up other players, and a run without a player is false.
The number of characters in the text (Unicode code points). Null for a non-text argument.

True when the whole text matches the regular expression (Java syntax). Use .* at either end for a partial match. Patterns up to 256 characters and texts up to 1024 characters; anything beyond those limits, or an invalid pattern, is false.
The largest of the given numbers. Null when any argument is not a number.
The smallest of the given numbers. Null when any argument is not a number.
The value as a number: a number as is, or text that reads as one. Null otherwise, including for booleans and for infinity.

A random number between the bounds: a whole number from min to max inclusive when both bounds are whole, otherwise a real from min up to max. Reversed bounds are swapped. This is the one function that is not pure: the same call can give different results.
Rounds to the nearest whole number, or to the given number of decimal places (0 to 15). Halves round away from zero.
True when the text begins with the prefix, case-sensitively. A non-text argument makes it false.
The text without leading and trailing whitespace. Null for a non-text argument.

items/ruby_sword.yml.raw:
# One file, one content type, many keyed resources (§7.2).
ruby_sword:
  template: base_item        # resolves in this pack's namespace
  material: NETHERITE_SWORD
  model: sample:ruby_sword_model
  display_name: "Ruby Sword"
  # a comment inside the definition must survive a round-trip
  lore:
    - "Burns with inner fire"
  future_component: { keep: me }
  mechanics:
    - durability:
        max: 500
    - soulbound: {}
    - commands:
        on_left_click:
          - "tellraw %player% {\"text\":\"The ruby hums.\",\"color\":\"red\"}"

blocks/chorus_pillar.yml.raw:
chorus_pillar:
  technique: chorus
  texture: block/chorus_pillar
  display_name: "Chorus Pillar"

blocks/ghost_panel.yml.raw:
# Technical technique: PDC-identified on an arbitrary vanilla host, no
# blockstate bits spent — the host carries the appearance.
ghost_panel:
  technique: technical
  host: bone_block
  texture: block/ghost_panel
  display_name: "Ghost Panel"

blocks/string_fence.yml.raw:
string_fence:
  technique: string
  texture: block/world_fence
  display_name: "String Fence"

furnitures/bench.yml.raw:
# The multi-seat sit fixture: two seat offsets, no storage — the right-click
# priority (ECA → storage → seat) only reaches sitPlayer on a storage-free
# cluster, and the seat flow needs the first *live* seat to be selectable
# (an occupied seat is skipped). qa furniture.seats drives it from a real
# client. Texture reuses the workbench png.
bench:
  texture: block/workbench
  display_name: Bench
  rotation: 90
  hitboxes:
    - type: barrier
      offset: [0, 0, 0]
      width: 1.0
      height: 0.6
    - type: interaction
      offset: [0, 0.4, 0]
      width: 1.4
      height: 1.0
  seats:
    - offset: [-0.3, 0.3, 0]
    - offset: [0.3, 0.3, 0]

furnitures/bloom.yml.raw:
# The evolution chain, terminal stage: no further evolution. See
# seedling.yml for the surface notes.
bloom:
  texture: block/workbench
  display_name: Bloom
  rotation: 90
  hitboxes:
    - type: interaction
      offset: [0, 0.5, 0]
      width: 1.0
      height: 1.0
  storage: 9

furnitures/crate.yml.raw:
# The storage-capacity probe: a 54-slot grid (the parser's ceiling — sizes
# are multiples of 9 from 9 to 54) with none of the other click consumers —
# no seats, no lights, no ECA rules — so a right-click goes straight to
# openStorage. qa furniture.storage-capacity drives it from a real client:
# menu scaling, full-grid addressing, per-cluster isolation, reload
# survival. Texture reuses the workbench png.
crate:
  texture: block/workbench
  display_name: Crate
  rotation: 90
  hitboxes:
    - type: interaction
      offset: [0, 0.5, 0]
      width: 1.0
      height: 1.0
  storage: 54

furnitures/lamp.yml.raw:
# The light-cells probe: two lights at different levels (per-cell levels +
# both cells riding the cluster's light record) and none of the other click
# consumers — no storage, no seats, no ECA rules — so a right-click falls
# through the whole priority chain. qa furniture.light-toggle drives it from
# a real client. Texture reuses the workbench png.
lamp:
  texture: block/workbench
  display_name: Lamp
  rotation: 90
  hitboxes:
    - type: interaction
      offset: [0, 0.5, 0]
      width: 1.0
      height: 1.0
  lights:
    - offset: [0, 1, 0]
      level: 8
    - offset: [1, 0, 0]
      level: 7

furnitures/seedling.yml.raw:
# The evolution chain, stage 1: seedling → sprout (after 180s) → bloom
# (after 330s — sprout restates it because stage clocks run from PLACEMENT,
# not from the previous stage). Storage-bearing so qa furniture.evolution
# can prove the grid rides the in-place transform, and the near-identical
# surfaces keep the shipped semantics visible: evolution changes ONLY the
# root's visual + id + stage count. Texture reuses the workbench png.
seedling:
  texture: block/workbench
  display_name: Seedling
  rotation: 90
  hitboxes:
    - type: interaction
      offset: [0, 0.5, 0]
      width: 1.0
      height: 1.0
  storage: 9
  evolution:
    - target: world:sprout
      after: 180
    - target: world:bloom
      after: 330

furnitures/signpost.yml.raw:
# The restricted-rotation probe: rotation: 0 disables the snap grid —
# snapYaw returns 0 whatever way the placer faces, so the light cell and
# the seat always land EAST of the anchor (their asymmetric offsets are
# what make a wrong rotation visible). qa furniture.rotation places it at
# an off-grid yaw and pins the unrotated result. Texture reuses the
# workbench png.
signpost:
  texture: block/workbench
  display_name: Signpost
  rotation: 0
  hitboxes:
    - type: interaction
      offset: [0, 0.5, 0]
      width: 1.0
      height: 1.0
  seats:
    - offset: [0.4, 0.3, 0]
  lights:
    - offset: [1, 0, 0]
      level: 7

furnitures/sprout.yml.raw:
# The evolution chain, stage 2: sprout → bloom (after 330s since the
# cluster's PLACEMENT — stage clocks are absolute, never per-stage
# relative). See seedling.yml for the surface notes.
sprout:
  texture: block/workbench
  display_name: Sprout
  rotation: 90
  hitboxes:
    - type: interaction
      offset: [0, 0.5, 0]
      width: 1.0
      height: 1.0
  storage: 9
  evolution:
    - target: world:bloom
      after: 330

furnitures/workbench.yml.raw:
workbench:
  # The full member surface: barrier collision + interaction hitbox,
  # a seat, a light cell, storage, a label and one timed evolution stage.
  texture: block/workbench
  display_name: Workbench
  rotation: 90
  hitboxes:
    - type: barrier
      offset: [0, 0, 0]
      width: 1.0
      height: 0.9
    - type: interaction
      offset: [0, 0.4, 0]
      width: 1.2
      height: 1.1
  seats:
    - offset: [0, 0.3, 0]
  lights:
    - offset: [0, 1, 0]
      level: 14
  storage: 9
  label: "&eWorkbench"
  evolution:
    - target: world:workbench_aged
      after: 3600

furnitures/workbench_aged.yml.raw:
# The evolution target of workbench — same members, older look.
workbench_aged:
  texture: block/workbench_aged
  display_name: "Weathered Workbench"
  rotation: 90
  hitboxes:
    - type: barrier
      offset: [0, 0, 0]
      width: 1.0
      height: 0.9
    - type: interaction
      offset: [0, 0.4, 0]
      width: 1.2
      height: 1.1
  seats:
    - offset: [0, 0.3, 0]
  lights:
    - offset: [0, 1, 0]
      level: 10
  storage: 9
  label: "&7Weathered Workbench"

items/crucible_blade.yml.raw:
# Custom durability showcase (qa mechanics.custom-durability): the mechanic
# owns wear in stack PDC — vanilla damage is cancelled and the third vanilla
# use breaks the blade. The right-click rule reads the live counters through
# ${item.*} interpolation, giving the QA run a chat-readable wear probe that
# doubles as the expression-surface check for the durability state.
crucible_blade:
  material: IRON_SWORD
  display_name: "Crucible Blade"
  behavior:
    - on: click:right
      do:
        - message: "blade-wear ${item.durability_used}/${item.durability_max}"
  mechanics:
    - durability:
        max: 3

items/feast_bread.yml.raw:
# Custom food showcase (qa mechanics.custom-food): nutrition, saturation and
# can_always_eat project onto the vanilla food component at stack build, so
# the eat itself is native vanilla logic with authored values. The effects
# list and the consume rule ride the PlayerItemConsumeEvent listeners. The
# QA run eats this at full hunger — only can_always_eat makes that possible.
feast_bread:
  material: BREAD
  display_name: "Feast Bread"
  behavior:
    - on: consume
      do:
        - message: "feast-devoured"
  mechanics:
    - food:
        nutrition: 6
        saturation: 12.0
        can_always_eat: true
        effects:
          - type: speed
            amplifier: 1
            duration_ticks: 200

items/light_snack.yml.raw:
# The can_always_eat gate (qa mechanics.custom-food): at full hunger this
# never becomes edible — the use aborts, no consume event fires, the item
# survives. Guards the negative half of the vanilla component projection.
light_snack:
  material: BREAD
  display_name: "Light Snack"
  behavior:
    - on: consume
      do:
        - message: "snack-devoured"
  mechanics:
    - food:
        nutrition: 2
        saturation: 2.0
        can_always_eat: false
        effects:
          - type: haste
            amplifier: 0
            duration_ticks: 100

items/ration.yml.raw:
# Food mechanic: the base material is edible (the 1.21.4 API has no
# consumable component surface yet), the component overrides nutrition.
ration:
  material: COOKED_BEEF
  display_name: "Wayfarer's Ration"
  mechanics:
    - food:
        nutrition: 8
        saturation: 12
        can_always_eat: true
        effects:
          - type: SPEED
            amplifier: 0
            duration_ticks: 400

items/satchel.yml.raw:
satchel:
  material: CHEST
  display_name: "Traveler's Satchel"
  mechanics:
    - backpack:
        rows: 2
        title: "&6Satchel"

items/storm_wand.yml.raw:
# ECA showcase: a condition, a rule cooldown, and the commands mechanic —
# one left-click drives both surfaces (qa mechanics.commands-and-cooldown):
# the console tellraw and the player-executed version marker fire on every
# swing while the rule's message is suppressed inside its 2s cooldown window.
storm_wand:
  material: BLAZE_ROD
  display_name: "Storm Wand"
  behavior:
    - on: click:left
      if:
        - "player.health > 0"
      cooldown: 3000
      do:
        - message: {text: "&bThe wand crackles."}
  mechanics:
    - commands:
        on_left_click:
          - "tellraw %player% {\"text\":\"The wand sparks.\",\"color\":\"aqua\"}"
    - commands:
        as_player: true
        on_left_click:
          - "materione version"

items/talisman.yml.raw:
talisman:
  material: NETHERITE_SWORD
  display_name: "Warden's Talisman"
  lore:
    - "Refuses to leave its owner"
  mechanics:
    - durability:
        max: 2000
    - soulbound: {}
